title: Number of Recent Calls
observed_problem_fact: Requests arrive with strictly increasing times and each call reports how many requests fall in a fixed trailing time window ending at the newest request
idea_used: Requests leave the window in arrival order, so a time-ordered queue drops the out-of-window prefix from its front
m3_applicability: One time-to-live and a clock that does not step back give deadlines in put order; the FIFO ring pops exactly the expired prefix, so size() and isEmpty() cost O(expired + 1) instead of a walk over every entry
target_owner: M3ExpiryOrderIndex ring mode, popped by M3PassiveExpiringMap.purge
compatibility_limit: The provider removes an entry when now >= deadline and never expires a negative deadline; the ring is kept only while deadlines do not decrease
read_scope: official problem statement only; no solution, editorial or submission code read or copied

title: Design Authentication Manager
observed_problem_fact: Tokens expire a fixed time after they are generated, renewal of an unexpired token restarts that time, and an expiry due at the current time happens before the other action at that time
idea_used: A renewal leaves the old expiry record behind; records are checked against the token's current expiry when they reach the front
m3_applicability: A put that changes an expiration time changes the slot stamp and appends a new record; records whose stamp differs are skipped at the front and dropped in one compaction pass when stale records outnumber current ones
compatibility_limit: Inclusive expiry at now >= deadline matches the provider; renewal of an expired key is a remove plus an insert, as in the provider's put
read_scope: official problem statement only; no solution, editorial or submission code read or copied

title: Sliding Window Maximum
observed_problem_fact: A window of fixed size slides over an array one position at a time and each position asks for the maximum inside the window
idea_used: Entries that can no longer matter are discarded lazily when they surface at the front of a monotonic queue instead of being searched for
m3_applicability: Removed or refreshed slots are never searched for in the index; their records die when they surface at the front, so remove() stays O(1) and purge pays only for records that reach the front
compatibility_limit: Stale records cost memory until compaction; compaction keeps the index at most about twice the expiring entries plus 64 records
read_scope: official problem statement only; no solution, editorial or submission code read or copied

title: Seat Reservation Manager
observed_problem_fact: Seats are numbered from one; reserving returns the smallest unreserved seat number and unreserving makes a seat available again
idea_used: A min-heap hands out the next minimum after arbitrary returns
m3_applicability: Per-entry policies or a clock that steps back produce deadlines out of order; the index then switches to a 4-ary min-heap over long[] due, int[] slot and int[] stamp lanes (the unrolled sorted ring is already a valid heap)
compatibility_limit: O(log n) per put and per expired entry in heap mode; the index returns to the ring when it empties
read_scope: official problem statement only; no solution, editorial or submission code read or copied
